key_insight: A genome-guided, physics-informed screening workflow can rapidly narrow thousands of lead-free double perovskite compositions to a few phase-stable semiconductors with strong optical properties.
engineering_relevance: This provides interpretable design rules for finding safer, stable absorber and sensing materials for all-inorganic photovoltaics and optoelectronics without relying on lead.
method: Built ML surrogates from 1,221 DFT-calculated A2BB'X6 compounds using four descriptor families: packing, bonding, polarization, and electronic identity.
Used a staged inverse-design filter to screen 13,088 charge-balanced lead-free compositions.
Validated shortlisted candidates with DFT and convex-hull stability checks.
evidence_signal: The stability classifier achieved ROC-AUC 0.92 and the band-gap regressor reached R2 = 0.93 on held-out data, and five candidates were DFT-validated on the convex hull.
watch_item: The shortlist is computationally validated, so experimental synthesis, phase purity, and long-term stability still need confirmation under real processing conditions.
paper_title: Genome-Guided Interpretable Screening of Phase-Stable, Lead-Free Double Perovskite Absorbers for All-Inorganic Semiconductors, Sensors, and Photovoltaics with DFT-Validated Design Rules
